mn1:1.2: On one occasion, the Auspicious One was dwelling at Ukkaṭṭhā, in the Subhaga Forest, at the root of a magnificent sal tree.
mn1:1.3: There, the Auspicious One addressed the monks:
mn1:2.1: “Monks, I will give you the teaching on the root of all things.
mn1:2.2: Listen to it and pay careful attention. I will speak.
mn1:3.1: “Monks, take an unlearned ordinary person who has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the nobles; one has not seen the righteous men, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the righteous men.
mn1:3.3: Perceiving earth as earth, he conceives earth, he conceives in arth, he conceives from earth, he conceives ‘earth is mine,’ he delights in earth.
mn1:3.4: What is the cause of that?
mn1:3.5: He has not understood it, I say.
mn1:4.2: Perceiving water as water, he conceives water, he conceives in water, he conceives from water, he conceives ‘water is mine,’ he delights in water.
mn1:4.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:4.4: He has not understood it, I say.
mn1:5.2: Perceiving fire as fire, he conceives fire, he conceives in fire, he conceives from fire, he conceives ‘fire is mine,’ he delights in fire.
mn1:5.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:5.4: He has not understood it, I say.
mn1:6.2: Perceiving air as air, he conceives air, he conceives in air, he conceives from air, he conceives ‘air is mine,’ he delights in air.
mn1:6.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:6.4: He has not understood it, I say.
mn1:7.2: Perceiving beings as beings, he conceives beings, he conceives in beings, he conceives from beings, he conceives ‘beings are mine,’ he delights in beings.
mn1:7.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:7.4: He has not understood it, I say.

mn1:8.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:8.4: He has not understood it, I say.

mn1:9.2: Perceiving the Overlord as the Overlord, he conceives the Overlord, he conceives in the Overlord, he conceives from the Overlord, he conceives ‘the Overlord is mine,’ he delights in the Overlord.

mn1:9.4: He has not understood it, I say.

mn1:10.4: He has not understood it, I say.

mn1:26.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:26.4: He has not understood it, I say.
mn1:27.1: Monks, a monk who is a trainee, who has not fulfilled his goal but lives aspiring to the supreme safety from the yoke, comprehends earth as earth.
mn1:27.2: Comprehending earth as earth, let him not conceive earth, let him not conceive in earth, let him not conceive from earth, let him not conceive ‘earth is mine,’ let him not delight in earth.
mn1:27.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:27.4: He ought to fully understand it, I say.

mn1:171.1: Monks, the Realized One, the Arahant, the Rightly Self-Awakened One, comprehends earth as earth.
mn1:171.2: Comprehending earth as earth, he does not conceive earth, he does not conceive in earth, he does not conceive from earth, he does not conceive ‘earth is mine,’ he does not delight in earth.
mn1:171.3: What is the cause of that?
mn1:171.4: Because he has seen that delight is the root of suffering—
mn1:171.5: that with being there is birth, and one who is ages and dies.
mn1:171.6: Therefore, monks, the Realized One—with the ending, fading away, cessation, giving up, and letting go of all cravings—has awakened with the supreme perfect awakening, I say.
